label: Vasco da Gama first India voyage
adaptation_note: Registered coast and outward/homeward route layers prevent route–shore mergers at native resolution. Six enlarged port windows, two Cape windows and a Madagascar reference preserve the source three ports, opposite directions and coastal/island context. Modern partial coast, displaced callout codes and introduced teaching tracks are explicitly qualified; no navigational accuracy.
acceptance_requirement: Keep the opposite itinerary directions, all source ports and coast/island context. Do not merge a route with its coastline.

frames.title: Shared coastal reference layer
frames.teaching_key: Selected partial modern European, African and western Indian coasts, with Madagascar southeast of Africa. Read by toggling with the outward and homeward route overview layers, which use the identical viewport and scale. Blank space is not a land/water classification; omitted coasts remain omitted. This layer has no itinerary or ports. North up. Uniform scale 0.112 native pins per source unit; centred layout focus (65, 22, 345, 290). No kilometre scale is inferred from these introduced projected coordinates. Features continuing across a viewport edge are not termini. The tiny closed island-location code is symbolic; the final enlarged Madagascar view supplies its actual outline.

source_window.rectangle_role: centred layout focus, not exact clipping rectangle

frames.title: Outward itinerary layer
frames.teaching_key: 1497–1499 first India voyage: outward Lisbon (upper left), south around Cape region, north to Malindi, then northeast to Calicut/Kozhikode (upper right). Three enlarged closed callouts are displaced source port-location codes; their coast-anchor leaders are omitted here and retained in port details; they are enlarged in the three following port windows. Direction chevrons lie on the itinerary. Toggle with the shared coastal layer to relate route and coast without merging the two. North up. Uniform scale 0.112 native pins per source unit; centred layout focus (65, 22, 345, 290). No kilometre scale is inferred from these introduced projected coordinates. Features continuing across a viewport edge are not termini. Port circles are recoded at radius 2 native pins and route under their interiors is suppressed; this changes glyph size only, not source location/order. Direction chevrons are recoded on the same two source corridors.

source_window.rectangle_role: centred layout focus, not exact clipping rectangle

frames.title: Outward Lisbon port detail
frames.teaching_key: Lisbon, outward itinerary. Closed callout and its short leader to the selected coast are from the source; the callout is displaced offshore for reading, not an exact harbour coordinate. The route meets the callout, not a falsely joined coastline. Cape is a rounding region, not a fourth port. North up. Uniform scale 0.5 native pins per source unit; centred layout focus (51.5, 22, 100, 68). No kilometre scale is inferred from these introduced projected coordinates. Features continuing across a viewport edge are not termini. Where present, the direction head is a smaller native open V at the same source tip, avoiding an artificial closed triangle.
